intro:
Use it to ask a question that has to be answered before anything else on the page: deleting a project, discarding changes, signing out of every device.

A press outside it, Escape and `AlertDialog.Cancel` all close it without doing anything, and `AlertDialog.Action` closes it once it has done its work. The question sits in a panel, and `AlertDialog.Footer` moves out of the panel into the darker band under it, where the answers sit side by side at equal widths.

For a task rather than a yes or no, such as a form to fill in, use [Dialog](/docs/web/components/dialog), or [Sheet](/docs/web/components/sheet) for a longer one. For a message that can wait on the page, use [Alert](/docs/web/components/alert).
usage:
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialog.Trigger render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>Delete project</AlertDialog.Trigger>
  <AlertDialog.Content tone="destructive">
    <AlertDialog.Title>Delete Orchard?</AlertDialog.Title>
    <AlertDialog.Description>Its 14 boards go with it.</AlertDialog.Description>
    <AlertDialog.Footer>
      <AlertDialog.Cancel />
      <AlertDialog.Action onClick={remove}>Delete project</AlertDialog.Action>
    </AlertDialog.Footer>
  </AlertDialog.Content>
</AlertDialog>

parts.Trigger: What opens the dialog. Pass your own button as `render`.
parts.Content: The dialog: a panel in a darker band, over a dimmed page. `tone` colours the media and sets the action's default colour, `size="sm"` centres a shorter question, and `blur` frosts the page behind it. Anything other than the footer, such as a field, goes in the panel.
parts.Media: A glyph in a disc of the dialog's tone, above the title.
parts.Title: The question. The dialog is announced by it.
parts.Description: What follows from each answer, read out after the title.
parts.Footer: The answers, side by side at equal widths in the band under the panel. It can sit at any depth inside `AlertDialog.Content`.
parts.Cancel: Closes the dialog and does nothing else. It reads "Cancel" unless given children.
parts.Action: Does what the dialog asks about, then closes it. It takes a [Button](/docs/web/components/button)'s props, a `tone`, and `variant="soft"` for an answer that is not the main one. When `onClick` returns a promise, it waits for it. `hold` makes it an action that must be pressed and held.

examples.title: With an icon
examples.description: `AlertDialog.Media` puts a glyph in a disc of the dialog's `tone` above the title. `size="sm"` makes the dialog narrower and centres the question over the two answers.

examples.title: Type to confirm
examples.description: Anything that is not the footer goes in the panel, here a field. The action stays `disabled` until the repository's name is typed, so a habit of pressing Enter cannot delete it. `dismissible={false}` keeps a press outside from throwing the typing away.

examples.title: While it works
examples.description: The action's `onClick` returns a promise. While it runs, the button shows a spinner and the dialog cannot be closed. It closes when the promise resolves. When it rejects, the dialog stays open, and here a plain [Alert](/docs/web/components/alert) in the panel says what went wrong. Turn on the switch to see the failure.

examples.title: Hold to confirm
examples.description: `hold={1500}` makes the action one that must be pressed and held for a second and a half while a fill runs across it. Letting go early drains it. Holding Space or Enter works the same way.

examples.title: Three answers
examples.description: A footer can hold more than two answers. Discard is an action with `tone="destructive"` and `variant="soft"`: a tint rather than a fill, so Save stays the one filled button.

notes:
### Closing

A press outside it, Escape and `AlertDialog.Cancel` close it, unless an action is running. `dismissible={false}` stops a press outside from closing it, for a question that a stray click should not answer; Escape still does. `AlertDialog.Action` closes it after its `onClick`, unless that handler calls `event.preventDefault()` or returns a promise that rejects.

### Focus

When it opens, focus moves to the first thing in it that takes focus: a field in the panel if there is one, otherwise the first answer. Put `AlertDialog.Cancel` first in the footer, so the answer focused by default is the one that changes nothing. Focus goes back to the trigger when it closes.

### Holding and screen readers

A screen reader cannot hold a button, so a press that arrives with no pointer or key going down first, as a screen reader's does, confirms straight away. The button is described as "Press and hold to confirm" for everyone else.

### Opening it from code

Pass `open` and `onOpenChange` to open it from anywhere, such as a menu item, without an `AlertDialog.Trigger`.
